name: Framer External Agents — Claude Code Gets Native Canvas, CMS, and Component Access
hook: Framer 3.0 shipped native External Agents support: Claude Code (plus Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI) connects directly to a Framer project's canvas, CMS collections, components, and styles — no manual MCP setup required. Framer's agent connection gives Claude Code full context to inspect layouts, clean up styles, write copy, manage CMS items, and generate new sections. The demo Framer highlighted: connecting Claude Code from the terminal, feeding a folder of CSV + Markdown + images, and having it build a fully-structured Framer CMS with collections, fields, references, and pages in one session.

name: Claude Code v2.1.237 — Built-In Concise Output Style Skips Preamble, Stays Thorough
hook: v2.1.237 (August 20) ships a built-in Concise output style selectable in `/config → Output style`. It cuts the preamble, narration, and filler sentences Claude typically leads with while keeping full technical depth — responses jump straight to the result. Distinct from existing custom styles: it requires no SKILL.md and isn't token-compressed (no caveman tradeoff), just purpose-driven prose. Pairs naturally with auto mode for a session that feels much more tool-like.

name: Claude Code v2.1.236–238 — keybindingFlavor Readline, headersHelper, macOS Sandbox, Memory Leak Patched
hook: Three releases Aug 19–20 tighten up the power-user surface: `keybindingFlavor: "readline"` (v2.1.238) makes Ctrl+W delete back to the previous whitespace Bash-style; `headersHelper` on plugin marketplace entries lets a command mint short-lived tokens for catalog and archive fetches; macOS wildcard read-deny rules (v2.1.236) now take precedence over allows and can't be bypassed by renaming (`**/.env` actually sticks). v2.1.238 also patches an unbounded memory growth bug in long interactive sessions — subagent tool results now release after leaving the display window, fixing runaway RAM on big multi-agent jobs.

name: 0xDarkMatter/claude-mods v3.7.0 — 103 Skills; New hono-ops and rembg-ops Drop
hook: v3.7.0 (August 2026) adds two production skills to the 103-skill library: `hono-ops` codifies Hono v4 on Cloudflare Workers — typed bindings, zValidator request validation, RPC, streaming, `onError` discipline, and test patterns under vitest-pool-workers; `rembg-ops` handles transparent-PNG cutouts with a deterministic model fallback ladder for non-photographic input. The collection also ships 13 output styles, 13 hooks, 14 rules, and 3 agent personas targeting real workflows from Python async to Rust ownership, AWS Fargate, and Craft CMS.

name: tonsofskills.com — Open-Source Marketplace: 471 Plugins, 3,069 Skills, 347 Agents, ccpi CLI
hook: jeremylongshore/claude-code-plugins-plus-skills is the largest community-curated index for Claude Code: 471 plugins, 3,069 skills, and 347 agents with an open-source marketplace at tonsofskills.com and a dedicated `ccpi` CLI package manager. Scored Grade A in the July 2026 community review. Production playbooks cover in-depth operational patterns for running Claude Code plugin infrastructure at scale — real-world code, checklists, and tested configurations, not demos.

name: wanshuiyin/Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep (ARIS) — ~14.9K Stars; Updated Aug 19; Autonomous ML Research Overnight
hook: ARIS is now 82 composable Claude Code skills (up from 80 in August 9 release) for autonomous overnight ML research — it reads papers, generates ideas, runs experiments, and rewrites manuscripts while GPT-5.6-Sol via Codex MCP acts as adversarial reviewer so the two models debate rather than self-agree. Updated August 19 (14.9K stars). Papers produced with ARIS accepted at AAAI 2026. No framework, no lock-in — plain Markdown works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, or any LLM agent.

name: JuliusBrussee/caveman — ~99K Stars; Day 27; 100K Milestone This Week
hook: ~99,000 stars and closing in on 100K — watch this space. Compresses agent responses into terse caveman-speak without losing technical accuracy; code, commands, and error messages remain byte-for-byte exact, only prose is stripped. 65% average output token reduction (range 22–87% across 1,200 test scenarios). The `/caveman-compress` companion shrinks CLAUDE.md and memory files by ~46%, saving input tokens on every future session.
